core.title: Keep every train-level acceptance well-formed
core.given: A train plan artifact (a train file, wherever the profile's plan-item pattern places train artifacts, flat or subject-nested) declares the optional acceptances[] block (WMBT acceptance shape); each entry contributes a derived repo rule via rule binding.
core.when: The planner authors, edits or keeps a train-level acceptance that is checked at CONFIRM.
core.then: Every train-level acceptance must be well-formed: identity.urn matches the acceptance URN grammar (acc:<train-id>:<slug>), identity.purpose is populated, identity.phase is one of RED|GREEN|SMOKE|REFACTOR, and the block is measurable via harness.type OR signal.metric together with signal.threshold.
prefer: Satisfy all four constraints: identity.urn matches the acc grammar (acc:<train-id>:<slug>); identity.purpose populated (becomes the derived rule's description); identity.phase in RED|GREEN|SMOKE|REFACTOR; measurable via harness.type OR signal.metric+signal.threshold.

Copy the exemplar: identity {urn: acc:train:self-compliance:validate-lifecycle:idempotent-on-retry, id: AC-SMOKE-001, purpose: 'Re-running the train with the same idempotency key produces no duplicate side effects', phase: SMOKE}, harness {type: e2e}, signal {metric: duplicate_side_effects_on_retry, threshold: 0}.
Let the rule id derive: acc:<train-id>:<slug> -> repo.<train-id>.acc-<slug>.
avoid: id: at acceptance-block top level (the rule id derives mechanically from the URN).

disposition: set by hand anywhere in the repository's rule-binding files (the declaration files from which rule binding derives repo rules; binding sets every derived repo rule's disposition to strict).
Retired URN schemes or examples failing the acc grammar / the train schema's acceptance shape.
signal.metric without signal.threshold (or vice versa) as sole measurability.
core.why: Each acceptance becomes a derived repo rule that rule binding sets to strict; a bad URN, missing purpose/phase or unmeasurable block yields an unbindable or meaningless rule, so a confirm-blocking check verifies well-formedness.
evidence: The well-formedness check passes at CONFIRM (confirm-blocking) over every selected train acceptance.
On failure the check reports the train artifact, the acceptance's URN, the failed constraint, and detail.
The authorable exemplar itself satisfies the acceptance URN grammar, parses as a valid parent train artifact, and validates against the train schema's acceptance definition.
Every constraint of the check has a fault-injection test; a clean run over an empty selection (no trains with acceptances) proves nothing.
verification: A well-formedness check over train plan artifacts runs at the CONFIRM phase and is confirm-blocking (it blocks the confirm on any finding).
Per-rule enforcement: severity 3, disposition strict — the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

Selection is by presence of an acceptances[] block in a train plan artifact (the artifacts matched by the profile's plan-item pattern), not by change: existing unchanged blocks are selected too; train plan artifacts without the block are out of scope (the block is optional), and non-train acceptance blocks (e.g. WMBT-level acceptances outside the train artifacts) are not selected.
Traversal: train plan artifact -> acceptances[] -> identity / harness / signal fields.

Constraints checked: identity.urn matches the acceptance URN grammar (the acc grammar, train-acceptance shape); identity.purpose populated (it becomes the derived rule's description); identity.phase populated (RED|GREEN|SMOKE|REFACTOR); EITHER harness.type OR (signal.metric AND signal.threshold) populated (measurability).

Excluded by this check: id at the acceptance-block top level (the rule id derives mechanically from the URN) and disposition set anywhere in the repository's rule-binding files (rule binding sets the derived repo rule's disposition to strict, so the check excludes the field rather than validating it).
On failure the check reports the train artifact, the acceptance URN, the failed constraint, and detail.
Every constraint of the check has a fault-injection test; a clean run over an empty selection (no train artifacts carrying acceptances) proves nothing.
The authorable exemplar is itself verified to satisfy the acceptance URN grammar, parse as a valid parent train artifact, and validate against the train schema's acceptance definition.

The scope over which a hand-set disposition is excluded: the repository's rule-binding files — the declaration files from which rule binding derives repo rules and over which it sets the derived disposition. For Bun this scope is every YAML file in the repository.

proposedKeys.meaning: The repository's rule-binding files: the declaration files from which rule binding derives repo rules and over which it sets the derived disposition; a hand-set disposition anywhere in them is overridden. For Bun this scope is every YAML file in the repository.
proposedKeys.bunValue: all repo YAML (every YAML file in the repository)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The Bun restriction scopes 'disposition' to 'anywhere in repo YAML' — a repository-wide declaration-format scope. suffix.plan_artifact covers only plan artifacts, and roots.*/layout.* describe trees and locations, so none of them names this file set; no existing key fits.

neutralityNotes: The acceptances[] block shape (identity/harness/signal fields), the phases RED|GREEN|SMOKE|REFACTOR and CONFIRM, the acc URN scheme and the repo-rule id derivation are treated as method-level (WMBT/ATDD) vocabulary, not stack specifics, so they stay in the core; the concrete grammar the check enforces is additionally supplied via urn.acceptance, and the train artifact location comes from layout.plan_item (the existing plan-artifact path key; no new key needed). The authorable exemplar (prefer[1]) contains no stack constructs and is kept verbatim for losslessness — bun.json itself remains the delivered reference example. What could not be made neutral: this rule's validator/test/family/template/variant ids and failure-evidence field names (bunOnly, per the closed not-profile-keys list), the walker module path and spec-version citations (§3.3, §4.3, §4.4, spec v12 — realization citations, kept in bun.json only), and the exemplar's concrete typed-train parser machinery (the general obligations — parse as a valid parent train artifact and validate against the train schema's acceptance definition — are kept in the core). 'anywhere in repo YAML' is expressed as 'anywhere in the repository's rule-binding files', a profile-backed scope (idiom.rule_binding_files, for Bun: every YAML file in the repository) so the restriction keeps its exact artifact-format scope under instantiation without the core naming a file format and without equating all repository artifacts with repository YAML; the key is proposed because no existing vocabulary key names the repository's declaration-format file set (suffix.plan_artifact covers only plan artifacts).
